title: Turkish Hazel: Old Turkish Hazels You Can Visit
meta_description: A hazel sixteen metres tall with a trunk 235 centimetres round. Five Turkish hazels mapped, in Paris, Vienna, Amsterdam and Bucharest.
intro: A hazel is supposed to be a shrub you can see over. The Turkish hazel puts up a single straight trunk instead and keeps going: the one in the Square du Temple in Paris stands sixteen metres tall with a trunk 235 centimetres around. The Amsterdam tree, planted in the Hortus in 1795, is called the oldest and thickest of its kind in the Netherlands by the Dutch tree foundation. Romania has only two officially protected specimens of Corylus colurna and one of them grows in Cismigiu in Bucharest. Vienna protected a pair in the Resselpark in 1972 for the way they match, though they went in seventeen years apart, in 1900 and 1917. The best line about any of them belongs to French regional television, which ran a news piece written in the voice of the hazel in Square Maurice-Gardette: I am 145, stop cracking my hazelnuts.
